author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs:
(a) Unqualified Rav Naḥman is bar Yaakov. Tosafot, Bava Batra 46b: Rav Naḥman son of Rav Ḥisda asked Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov, 'Let our teacher instruct us: may a sharecropper testify?' Rav Yosef sat before him and said, 'Thus Shemuel said.' Tosafot writes that throughout the Gemara unqualified Rav Naḥman is Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov. Proof: he is never named with his father except where another Rav Naḥman appears alongside him, as here—the son of Rav Ḥisda—and Sanhedrin 8a, 24b; Ketubbot 104b; see there. Or Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, Tosafot Eruvin 43b. Ḥezkat HaBatim 52a: R. Ḥiyya of Hormiz spoke to Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak in Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov's name. I shall list many places below with Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak alongside unqualified Rav Naḥman, without calling the latter Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov. In the Jerusalem Talmud Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov repeatedly disagrees with Rav Sheshet; Babylonian Yoma 6b has Rav Naḥman and Rav Sheshet disagree. He is thus our Gemara's unqualified Rav Naḥman, Rav Sheshet's disputant, contrary to Rashi's apparent view in Gittin 31b that unqualified Rav Naḥman is Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, son-in-law of the nasi's household, as HaOr VeHaRotev 124a proves. There Rav Naḥman asked Ulla whether R. Yoḥanan had said this. Ulla answered yes. Rav Naḥman swore that even if R. Yoḥanan told him personally, he would not obey. When R. Oshaya went up, he told R. Ammi Ulla's report and Rav Naḥman's answer. Ammi said, 'Because Rav Naḥman is the nasi's son-in-law, does he slight R. Yoḥanan's teaching?'

Furthermore, Gittin 39b: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says he says the law does not follow the view, but rabbis arriving from Meḥoza report R. Zeira in Rav Naḥman's name that it does. Thus the two Rav Naḥmans differ. Eruvin 43b—and Bava Batra 152a—has Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak sitting behind Rava, and Rava before Rav Naḥman. Rava repeatedly reports Rav Naḥman, while Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak was Rava's student, as Lo Yaḥpor indicates. End of Tosafot, Bava Batra. Gittin there: Rava and Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak sat as Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov passed in a golden litter beneath a leek-green cloak. Rava approached; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak did not. He told Rava, 'Perhaps he belongs to the exilarch's household; Rava needs them, but I do not.' Rashi explains Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak was the nasi's son-in-law, as HaOr VeHaRotev. On recognizing Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov, he approached.

Tosafot there says Rashi interpreted Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak as unqualified Rav Naḥman, the exilarch's son-in-law. Maharshal's responsum likewise calls the HaOr VeHaRotev figure the exilarch's son-in-law; see Abba Mari the exilarch, whose son-in-law was Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak. But HaOr VeHaRotev says the nasi's household, as does Rashi. Rava's remark about Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov perhaps being of the exilarch's household likewise suggests a distinction. Mi SheAḥazo: the exilarch's household distressed R. Amram the pious; Yalta heard. Rashi calls her Rav Naḥman's wife, the nasi's daughter, wife of the court's head and important (see above). Tosafot Ein Tzadin calls her the exilarch's daughter. HaMokher Et HaBayit: Rav Huna tells Rav Naḥman he is close to the exilarch's gate; Rashbam calls Rav Naḥman the nasi's son-in-law, accustomed to judges. Rashi, Asarah Yuḥasin, says Rav Naḥman, Yalta's husband, was the nasi's son-in-law and judge for the exilarch. Thus she truly was the nasi's daughter; her husband was court head under the exilarch, making her important there. Tosafot Gittin concludes: unqualified Rav Naḥman is Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov, Rav Sheshet's colleague; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak needed no help from the household because he was wealthy.

I shall give clear proofs for Tosafot that unqualified Rav Naḥman is bar Yaakov, not bar Yitzḥak. Berakhot 61a and Eruvin 18b: Rav Naḥman says Manoaḥ was ignorant; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objects. Thus they differ, as Tosafot says. Pesaḥim 40b [Heilprin cites 40a]: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehudah reports Rav Naḥman reporting Shemuel; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak asks Rav Huna, 'Does the master say?' Shabbat 57b: Rav Naḥman reports Shemuel; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says the Mishnah supports it. Eruvin 72b: Rav Naḥman rules like Rav Yehudah HaSabbar [Rashi explains the epithet as referring to his sharpness]; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak cites Mishnah support. Yoma 54a: Rav Naḥman says, 'The sages say,' etc.; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says, 'We too have learned.' Shabbat 69b: Rav Naḥman reports Rabbah bar Avuhah; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objects. Niddah 16a: they ask Rav Naḥman; in that discussion Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak speaks. Likewise Bava Metzia 93a. Yevamot 101b: Rava reports Rav Naḥman’s ruling that ḥalitzah requires three and then raises a question; rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says. As above in HaShole'aḥ and Mi SheHotzi'uhu; Ein Tzadin 25a: Rav Naḥman speaks, an objection is raised, and rather Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says. There 26b: Rabbah bar Rav Huna expounds; Rav Naḥman says, 'My father taught,' etc.; Abaye favors Rabbah bar Rav Huna, then Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak speaks. This proves that even alongside Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, Rav Naḥman remains unqualified, contrary to Tosafot's explanation that Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov is specified when another Rav Naḥman appears, namely son of Rav Ḥisda or Rav Yitzḥak. Nevertheless, unqualified Rav Naḥman clearly is not bar Yitzḥak.

Gittin 67b: the exilarch's household distressed Rav Amram the pious; Yalta heard. Rashi calls her Rav Naḥman's wife, the nasi's daughter, wife of the court head and important, as HaOr VeHaRotev. Ein Tzadin 25b [Heilprin cites the end of 25a]: Rav Naḥman permitted Yalta to go in a litter. Rashi: his wife. Tosafot asks: this is permitted only for public need. Perhaps she too went for public need, as the exilarch's daughter whom many needed. End of quotation. This requires examination: Tosafot and Rashi above call her the nasi's daughter. Sukkah 10b: Rav Ḥisda and Rabbah bar Rav Huna visited the exilarch; Rav Naḥman housed them in a sukkah. Rashi says Rav Naḥman was court head, directing and commanding in the exilarch's house. Rav Naḥman visited Sura; Rav Ḥisda and Rabbah bar Rav Huna visited him, Sukkah 14b; they said Rav and Shemuel's ruling had been uprooted, Shevuot 48b. Sukkah 31a: an old woman complained to Rav Naḥman that the exilarch and all his rabbis sat in a stolen sukkah. Berakhot 51b: Ulla visited Rav Naḥman. After eating and Grace, Rav Naḥman asked him to send Yalta the blessing cup; he refused. In anger she broke four hundred wine jars and sent Ulla a message about itinerant people and words, etc. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak is mentioned immediately afterward. Thus Yalta, unqualified Rav Naḥman's wife, was the nasi's daughter.

In my opinion, Yevamot 80b says Rabbah bar Avuhah asked the rabbis to examine whether Rav Naḥman's flesh gave off vapor, so he might give him his daughter: Rav Naḥman had only sparse beard growth here and there. The epistle of R.Sh.G. [רש״ג; provisionally Rav Sherira Gaon] says he descended from him and from David; the nesi'im descended from David. Thus Yalta was Rabbah bar Avuhah's daughter. Shalshelet HaKabbalah 35 writes Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, following Rashi's identification. But unqualified Rav Naḥman repeatedly reports Rabbah bar Avuhah, whom Tosafot calls his teacher (see his entry), while Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak reports him only once. The former is therefore more plausibly his son-in-law. Some support is that Rav Naḥman had a son Rabbah, perhaps named for his father-in-law.

Bava Batra 65a: Rav Naḥman asked Rav Huna whether the law follows us or you; Rav Huna answered, 'You, since you are close to the exilarch's gate, where judges abound.' Rashbam: 'you' means Shemuel and his student Rav Naḥman; the nasi's son-in-law regularly saw judges and daily cases. Ketubbot 10(94b): Rami and Mar Ukva, Ḥama's sons, came before Rav Sheshet and Rav Naḥman. Rav Naḥman told Rav Sheshet, 'I am a judge'—by the exilarch and academy—'and you are not.' Bava Batra 151a has a similar matter and another incident. Sanhedrin 5: 'Someone like me judges monetary cases alone.' Bekhorot 37a: 'Someone like me, a sage,' etc. Bava Metzia 66a: everyone is a child compared with him in monetary law. Bava Kamma 96b: he told Rava not to speak while he judged, because our colleague Huna had said that Rav Naḥman and King Shapur—Shemuel—were peers in judicial law. He calls Rav Huna our colleague repeatedly; see his entry. Thus this expert judge and nasi's son-in-law was Rav Huna and Rav Sheshet's colleague.

Ein Tzadin 25a: Rav Naḥman says our colleagues—Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda—fell into great difficulties. Rashi says Rav Naḥman, Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda were all Rav's students. Rava was Rav Ḥisda's student; how could Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, on Rashi's view Rav Ḥisda's colleague, be student of Rava, his colleague's student? Moreover, unqualified Rav Naḥman would then be Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak, student of Rav and Shemuel. Rav died 4003, Rava 4111; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak headed the academy after Rava. Presumably grown when studying under Rav, he would die about 130 or older. Avodah Zarah 63a: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak reports Rav Ḥisda, apparently his teacher; Rav Ḥisda was unqualified Rav Naḥman's colleague. Hence they differ.

Asarah Yuḥasin 70a: a man summoned Rav Yehudah of Pumbedita before Rav Naḥman at Nehardea. Rav Yehudah consulted Rav Huna whether to go. Rav Huna said he need not, being a great man—greater than Naḥman, head at Pumbedita. Rashi, Sanhedrin 32, calls Pumbedita the Exile, Babylonia's principal academy, while Rav Naḥman was in Nehardea. Arukh, second entry Nahar, likewise places Rav Naḥman there. Yuḥasin, chronological amoraim list, places him at Shilḥi and Meḥoza with the Nehardean rabbis; we do not find him entering before Rav Huna, whom he called colleague. Nevertheless, for the nasi's household's honor—Rashi: its judge and the nasi's son-in-law—he should go. He found Rav Naḥman building, etc. Rav Naḥman asked him to send greetings to Yalta and spoke of his daughter Donag, etc. Thus Yalta's husband headed Nehardea. Yuḥasin, citing Dorot Olam and the epistle of R.Sh.G. [רש״ג; provisionally Rav Sherira Gaon], gives Pumbedita's succession: Rav Yehudah, Rabbah, Rav Yosef, Abaye, Rava, then Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak did not head Nehardea. How could he be the Rav Naḥman before whom Rav Yehudah was summoned there? This is an unanswerable proof for Tosafot's bar Yaakov identification. Mo'ed Katan 28a: dying Rav Naḥman asked Rava to tell the Angel of Death not to pain him. After death he told Rava he had suffered no pain, but would decline even God's offer to return, because fear of the Angel was so great. This too proves they differ: Rava's teacher Rav Naḥman died in Rava's lifetime, while Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak headed the academy after Rava's death.

One might find some support for Rashi. Kiddushin 33a: Abaye extended his hand for elders to lean on; Rava sent agents to extend theirs, rather than himself. Rav Naḥman sent eunuchs—Rashi: attendants always before him, a dignitary, nasi's son-in-law and court head, enforcing judgment; he sent them to support passing elders rather than do it himself and diminish his Torah's honor. He said, 'Without Torah, how many Naḥmans son of Abba are in the marketplace?' See Abaye above. Placing Abaye and Rava before Rav Naḥman seems to require bar Yitzḥak, Rava's student. Responsa Ḥut HaShani says there were two unqualified Rav Naḥmans: Rashi's Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak or Tosafot's Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov, and the Kiddushin figure, bar Abba. Unless 'son of Abba' is forced to mean 'son of their father,' which is strained; two Rav Naḥmans is less difficult. End of quotation. See below, Rav Naḥman bar Abba. This resolves my objection to Abaye and Rava being placed first. But Rashi calls him a dignitary, nasi's son-in-law and court head; both unqualified Rav Naḥman and Rav Naḥman bar Abba would then hold those same roles, which is implausible. Rather, the order reflects increasing elevation: Abaye helped himself; Rava sent agents, perhaps his students, since R. Elyakim was his attendant-student; Rav Naḥman acted loftily and sent eunuchs.

(b) Yalta brought blood before Rabbah bar bar Ḥana, then Rav Yitzḥak son of Rav Yehudah, Niddah 20b. Tosafot suggests she did not approach her husband Rav Naḥman because he might lack expertise; perhaps he feared error and would be stringent. Rav Huna's wife, after Rav Huna's death, had a case before Rav Naḥman. He wished to stand because a colleague's wife is like a colleague, but had his attendant throw a gosling toward him so the other litigant's arguments would not be obstructed, Shevuot 30b. Rav Naḥman asked Rav Yitzḥak for a blessing. He compared him to a tree: he already had children, Torah and wealth; may his offspring be like him, Ta'anit 5b. This might support Rashi's bar Yitzḥak, wealthy enough to need no help from the nasi's household, as Tosafot above. Yet Rav Naḥman truly was wealthy: Yalta broke four hundred jars, and Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov traveled in a golden litter and green cloak.

Rav Naḥman told his slave Daru to rouse him during the first verse, Berakhot 13b; to insulate cold water, Shabbat 51a. R. Ammi heard and objected; Rav Yosef asked why. He also spoke to him, Arvei Pesaḥim 116a. He sent Ḥama bar Adda, Zion's emissary, to R. Yaakov bar Idi; R. Yaakov bar Idi died before he arrived, and he found R. Zerika, Beitzah 25b. Pesaḥim 40a: Rabbah said a scrupulous person should not soak grain; Rav Naḥman asked who would heed Abba—an honorific for Rabbah—since Rav Huna and Rava bar Avin soaked it. At Shekhantziv he announced, 'Who will be mine for a day?' Yoma 18b; Yevamot 37b. He decreed a fast, prayed, and rain did not come. He said to take Naḥman and throw him from the wall to the ground; he became distressed and rain came, Ta'anit 24a.

Rav Yosef said Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak expounded these verses like Sinai, Kiddushin 20b. Maharshal notes that another book lacks bar Yitzḥak. Why erase it? Perhaps because Mo'ed Katan 12a and Eruvin 30a have Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak call Rav Yosef Sinai, according to Rashi; how could Yosef give him his own praise? Or Rav Yosef reports Rav Naḥman, Ta'anit 30b, and sat before him, Bava Batra 46b, apparently as student. Rav Yosef taught Rava, who taught Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak; how could he call his student's student Sinai? I then examined Ḥokhmat Shelomoh: another book lacks bar Yitzḥak; it must be unqualified Rav Naḥman, otherwise Tosafot at the end of Kol HaGet, calling Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak Rav Ashi's colleague—this is not there; see Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak below—would be difficult. He was junior to Rava, sitting behind him; how could Rav Yosef, his teacher's teacher, praise him? End of quotation. I rejoiced to agree with him. Rav Yosef could rightly call his teacher, unqualified Rav Naḥman, Sinai. Yet Heilprin reports that Arakhin 30b and Arukh, San, also name Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak in Rav Yosef’s praise. [The consulted digital Arakhin has bare Rav Naḥman.] It is difficult to emend three coincident errors.

Rav Naḥman said his father was among Mar Shemuel's judicial scribes. On Tosafot's view this is Yaakov, as Yuḥasin writes; Yuḥasin also calls Rav Yitzḥak Shemuel's scribe, see Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak below. He instituted the hesset oath, Shevuot 40b. Arukh explains it as heaviness, imposing an oath; some as advice, from 'if he entice you'; Ran as enticement by the court to swear. Rav Naḥman said, 'If Messiah is among the living, it is I,' Ḥelek 98b. Be'er Sheva: if there is a living example, such as myself, ruler with a rod to discipline, the exilarch's son-in-law. Ḥiddushei Aggadot calls him the exilarch's son-in-law—above, the nasi's—and of David's descendants. Perhaps he too descended from David, or feared sin, as the end of Sotah; see my discussion under Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak. Or Messiah judges truly by scent; this was Naḥman's excellence: all were children beside him in law; the law follows him in monetary matters; he judged alone, as above.

(c) Shemuel was his teacher: Rav Naḥman expounded in 'our teacher's' name, Shemuel, and 'our colleague's,' Ulla, Berakhot 38b. Rav Naḥman—or some say Rav Bivi bar Abaye—said, etc. Rav Naḥman expounded in our teacher's name, 'namely'—this should be the reading—Shemuel. He afterward appointed a public interpreter and announced that his earlier statement was mistaken, Eruvin 16b. Shemuel said, Ḥullin 54a; Ketubbot 10a; Yoma 83b. Rava was his student (see his entry). Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak sat behind Rava, Rava before Rav Naḥman bar Yaakov, as above. Rav Naḥman said, Rava objected, and Naḥman answered that he had intended to act thus but now, because 'you objected, and Rav Hamnuna objected at Sura,' he would not, Bava Batra 31b. This too distinguishes him from Rava's student bar Yitzḥak, who should have said 'the master objected.' Rava said not to hang empty jars upon Rav Naḥman—attribute unfounded claims to him—Bava Batra 7a, קג״א b [irregular source locator]; Avodah Zarah 37b; Ḥullin 50.

(d) Between Rav Naḥman and Rav Huna, the law follows Rav Huna in prohibitions and Rav Naḥman in monetary law (see his entry). Sefer Keritot, Yemot Olam, gate 3§21, gives Rav Sheshet in prohibitions and Rav Naḥman in monetary law. Rosh, HaZahav, limits the monetary rule to disagreement with Rav Sheshet. Shakh, Ḥoshen Mishpat 66 §122 [Heilprin cites 67], objects: it applies against any disputant; likewise Tosafot HaUmanin. See Responsa רמ״ע111 [abbreviated attribution held], and Beit Yaakov§11's objections to Shakh, at length, and responses. These rules concern one against one, not against two; see Tosafot Niddah 8 and Avodah Zarah 31, 'They do not disagree.' Responsa Ḥavvot Yair says the Shas often rules contrary to a general rule. Why then does Bava Metzia 110 object to ruling like Rav Kahana because we hold like Rav Naḥman?
(e) He died in 4079 (see part 1). His burial is at Kefar Bar'am—גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael].

(f) Rav Naḥman's daughters stirred a pot with their hands. Rav Ilish thought them righteous. They were captured with him; he heard one tell the other to ask their captor to take them farther away so they would not be redeemed, etc. Their stirring was by sorcery, Gittin 45a. Gilgulei Neshamot, letter bet §10, writes: they were Lot's two daughters who remained in Sodom, as 'he spoke to his sons-in-law, takers of his daughters,' etc., and seemed a jester. They remained from sexual desire and lewdness; such were their deeds now. Rav Ilish repairs Bela king of Sodom: they were captured by the angels, and he escaped through Abraham's merit, likened to a dove; his companions drowned and were not saved. Likewise Rav Ilish, his repair, escaped while others did not. Since he entered a marriage connection with Abraham, he made an awakening, and was now repaired in Rav Ilish. End of quotation. Yalta is Ma'akhah's reincarnation (see her entry).

(g) Abba bar Avimi, in his time. R. Abba asked him. Abaye in his name, his student. Avimi bar Pappa. Avimi bar Pappi. R. Adda bar Ahavah said, and in his name. Adda bar Avimi. R. Adda bar Mattanah. Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov. In R. Aḥa bar Ḥanina's name. Rav Aḥa bar Huna spoke to him. Rav Aḥa bar Minyomi in his name. Rav Aḥa bar Naḥman. Rav Aḥadvui son of Rav Mattanah. Eivo. R. Idit in his time. R. Ammi (see above). Amemar in his name. R. Assi, his colleague. He spoke to Rav Ashi—see Rav Ḥanan of Meḥoza, for it is a scribal error. Rav Bivi, his student. Rav Bivi bar Avin before him. Rav Bizna in his time. Rav Giddel bar Minyomi before him. Rav Dimi bar Yosef in his name and asking him. Hon his son asked him. Rav Huna, his colleague (see above). Rav Huna bar Ḥanina said: Rav Naḥman said. Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya before him. Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya, Levi's father, disagrees with him and was before him. Rav Huna bar Ḥelev asked him. Rav Huna son of R. Yehudah said: Rav Naḥman said. In R. Huna bar Natan's name. Rav Hamnuna spoke to him. Rav Zevid in his name. Mar Zutra bar Tovya said: Rav Naḥman said. Mar Zutra son of Rav Naḥman in his name. R. Zeira said: Rav Naḥman said, Rosh HaShanah 20b [irregular numeral in Heilprin]; Ketubbot 98a; Bava Batra 12a. Zeira asked him. Zeiri said. Ḥagga taught. He spoke to R. Ḥiyya son of Rav Mattanah. R. Ḥiyya of Hormiz in his name. Ḥiyya bar Ammi. R. Ḥiyya bar Abba. R. Ḥiyya Peraza'ah. R. Ḥiyya bar Yosef before him. Ḥama bar Adda, Zion's emissary (see above). R. Ḥama, Ḥasa's daughter's son. R. Ḥanina Ḥozna'ah in his time. Abba Ḥanan in his time. Ḥasa, his teacher—requires examination. Rav Ḥisda, his colleague (see above). Tavi raised a contradiction before him. Rav Tavla went to him. Rav Tovi bar Mattanah came before him. R. Yeiva the elder asked him. Rav Yehudah (see above). In R. Yoḥanan's name, Shabbat 146b. Rav Yosef bar Minyomi. Rav Yosef bar Ḥama said: Rav Naḥman said. Rav Yosef said: Rav Naḥman said (see above). In R. Yaakov's name. R. Yitzḥak blessed him (see above). He reported in R. Yitzḥak’s name, with an alternate attribution to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, Shabbat 131b. R. Yitzḥak bar Shemuel bar Marta before him. R. Yitzḥak son of R. Yehudah (see above). He sent to R. Yirmeyah bar Abba. Rav Naḥman said: R. Meir used to say, Ketubbot 85; Gittin 3, 23, 26; Bava Kamma 3. In R. Mani's name. R. Minyomi, his colleague. R. Menashya bar Yaakov in his time. Mar bar Yishmael objects—requires examination. Mar son of Ravina in his name. Neḥemyah bar Ḥanilai, his student. Rav Naḥman son of Rav Ḥisda told him, 'Let our teacher instruct us.' He became angry with Rav Seḥora. Rav Safra, his colleague. Ulla, his colleague (see above); he objected to Ulla, Zevaḥim 15a; Ḥullin 76b, and is called Mar (see above). Ulla bar Ila'ah before him. R. Ilai, Rabbah's father, before him. R. Ukva bar Ḥama objected to him. Rav Ukva bar Abba objected to him. R. Eina the elder spoke to him. R. Amram in his name. R. Amram the pious before him. Rav Anan (see above). Rav Pappa bar Shemuel before him. He said: Rav said, Sotah 12b; Pesaḥim 13a, 45b, 110b; Bekhorot 23b. Rav was his teacher (see above). Rava, his student (see above). Rabbah objected, Beitzah 32b; Ḥagigah 19a. He called Rabbah Abba (see his entry). Rabbah bar Natan. In Rabbah bar bar Ḥana's name, Bava Kamma 100b; see above. Rabbah bar Shila said: Rav Naḥman said. Rabbah son of Rav Huna said: Rav Naḥman said. Rabbah bar Avin. Rabbah Zuti spoke to him. Rabbah bar Avuhah, his teacher (see above). He called Rava son of Rav Huna Zuta Abba. Rabbah bar Ḥanina before him. Rami bar Shemuel spoke to him. Rami came before him. Rami bar Ḥama said: Rav Naḥman said, and objected to him. Rav Sheva. Rav Sheizvi said: Rav Naḥman said. R. Shila said. Shemuel, his teacher (see above). R. Shemuel bar Bisna said: Rav Naḥman said. Rav Sheshet, his colleague (see above).
